shock.title: Three food-price spikes since 2007, each peak higher than the last
shock.subtitle: FAO Food Price Index, all foods, monthly, Jan 1990 to Mar 2026.
legend: Shock month: prices more than 20% above a year earlier
shock.take: Each shock lasted more than a year, and prices have not gone back to the 2014–16 base.
notes: Peak **132.7** in Jun 2008; oils rose 109% on a year earlier.
2021–22 surge and the war in Ukraine
Record **160.2** in Mar 2022, the highest since 1990. Still **128.5** in Mar 2026.
shock.source: **Source:** FAO Food Price Index (2014–16 = 100). Shock months computed from year-on-year change.

drivers.title: Vegetable oils led two of the three shocks; meat never rose more than 28%
drivers.subtitle: Largest rise on a year earlier for each FAO food group during each shock period.
drivers.take: Oils and cereals moved most in every shock, so they are the two prices the warning watches.
notes: Never more than +28%, so it adds little warning.
drivers.source: **Source:** FAO Food Price Index sub-indices, monthly. Shock periods as defined on the previous page.

exposure.title: 20 of 91 countries pair serious hunger with high food-import reliance
exposure.subtitle: Each dot is a country. These countries buy much of their food abroad, so a global spike reaches hungry households.
legend: Exposed: GHI 20+ and above-median food imports
exposure.take: These 20 countries are where to prepare first when the signal appears.
exposure.source: **Sources:** Global Hunger Index 2025; World Bank, food imports (% of merchandise imports), latest year 2015–2024. **Note:** median food-import share 16.3%.

warning.title: Oils and cereals rose 20% before every food-price shock since 2000
warning.subtitle: Year-on-year change, Jan 2000 to Mar 2026, with the two-price signal below.
legend: Signal: both 20%+ above a year earlier
warning.take: No signal now: oils +13% and cereals +1% in Mar 2026.
notes: A shock followed 1 to 5 months later.
The 2002 signal was not followed by a shock.
The rule was read off this same history; models trained before 2013 missed most of 2020–21.
warning.source: **Source:** FAO Food Price Index, monthly. Signal: oils and cereals both more than 20% above a year earlier, outside a shock.
